'''Donald W. Braben''' was a British [[author]] and [[Professor|Honorary Professor]] in the Office of the Vice-Provost (Research), [[University College London]].<ref name="bsr">{{cite web |url=http://www.es.ucl.ac.uk/research/blueskies/braben.html |title=Donald Braben UCL Earth Sciences - UCL - Blue Skies Research |access-date=26 July 2011}}</ref>

==Life==
Braben was educated at the [[University of Liverpool]] where he was awarded a [[PhD]] in 1962 for work on [[Isotopes of sodium]].<ref name="braben">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Donald W.|last=Braben |title=Energy Levels of Na 23 |publisher=University of Liverpool |date=2012 |url=http://www.theses.com|author-link=Donald Braben}}{{subscription required}}</ref> He gained a pilot licence with the [[University Air Squadron]], which he maintained throughout his life.<ref name="Times obituary">https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/professor-don-braben-89-champion-of-scientific-inquiry-who-promoted-blue-skies-research-8cj8tpm8v</ref>

At university he married Shirley, a fellow PhD; they later had three children. Braben died in 2025, aged 89.<ref name="Times obituary" />

==Research==
Braben was a well-known critic of [[peer review]] and an advocate of [[blue skies research]], scientific freedom<ref>{{cite book |author=Donald W. Braben |title=Scientific freedom: the elixir of civilization |publisher=Wiley-Interscience |location=New York |year=2008 |isbn=978-0-470-22654-4 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Augsdorfer | first1 = P. | title = Scientific Freedom: The Elixir of Civilization. By Donald W. Braben | doi = 10.1002/cbic.200800670 | journal = ChemBioChem | volume = 9 | issue = 17 | pages = 2889–2890 | year = 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author=Braben, D. W. |title=Pioneering research: a risk worth taking |publisher=Wiley-Interscience |location=New York |year=2004 |isbn=0-471-48852-6 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Braben | first1 = D. | doi = 10.1016/S0378-4371(02)01065-8 | title = Blue Skies Research and the global economy | journal = Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications | volume = 314 | pages = 768–773| year = 2002 | issue = 1–4 |bibcode = 2002PhyA..314..768B }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Braben | first1 = D. W. | title = Innovation and academic research | doi = 10.1038/316401a0 | journal = Nature | volume = 316 | issue = 6027 | pages = 401–402 | year = 1985 |bibcode = 1985Natur.316..401B }}</ref> and the culture of science.<ref>{{cite book |author=Braben, D. W. |title=To be a scientist |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford [Oxfordshire] |year=1994 |isbn=0-19-852290-8 |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/tobescientist00brab }}</ref>  Braben was the author of ''To Be a Scientist: The Spirit of Adventure in Science and Technology'', (OUP 1994), ''Pioneering Research: A Risk Worth Taking'' (Wiley 2004) ''Scientific Freedom: The Elixir of Civilization'' (Wiley 2008), and ''Promoting the Planck Club: How defiant youth, irreverent researchers and liberated universities can foster prosperity indefinitely'' (Wiley 2014). ''Scientific Freedom: The Elixir of Civilisation'' was republished by Stripe Press in 2020 with a new Introduction.

Braben tried to persuade universities to recreate the success he had with the BP-sponsored Venture Research Unit (1980–90), and later at University College London from 2009. Venture Research is research that has a good chance of radically changing the way we think in an important field and is selected in face-to-face discussion.
